bull.b: Rapid gains in market share and prescriber adoption indicate that neffy is expanding beyond early users and gaining commercial relevance. Continued penetration among high-value prescribers could support durable revenue growth as the fully deployed sales force builds prescribing habits.

Material revenue growth combined with a high gross margin suggests the product has attractive underlying economics once commercial scale improves. This provides room to fund selling efforts and retain meaningful contribution from future sales, despite current corporate costs.

A defined reduction in cash-based spending can extend the company’s operating runway and improve the path from commercial growth to sustainable cash generation. The plan also signals greater prioritization of high-value prescribers rather than broad, less efficient promotion.

bear.b: The current revenue base remains far too small to support the company’s cost structure, producing substantial recurring losses. Unless commercial growth and planned expense reductions close this gap, earnings volatility will remain high and additional funding may be needed.

Persistent cash outflows show that the business is not yet financing operations internally, making liquidity dependent on available funding and successful execution. Continued burn reduces flexibility to invest in growth, absorb setbacks, or reach breakeven without capital actions.

The very thin equity cushion leaves the company exposed to refinancing and dilution risk if losses continue. High leverage also constrains strategic flexibility, because a larger share of future resources may need to support obligations rather than commercial expansion or pipeline development.
